disposition_reason: The review-layer method is safely definable without inventing a device command: bind each physical receptacle through its controller/hubs/MCU to an approved traceable fixture, collect complete USB descriptors/tree/events, verify its signed generation and negotiated speed, and run only a fixture-specific bounded non-destructive function supplied at execution. ED-03/05/06 allow topology, fixture, per-port speed and functional oracle as runtime inputs. ED-02/04 retain Source Key/Variant isolation because the shared code also names firmware flashing.
decision_basis: XLSX row 2203, same-row DeepSeek columns, GPT V2, historical record, duplicate-code identity and ED-01 through ED-30 were reviewed; actual next formal row Functionality 2204 / Wistron-BMC-00485-V003 / c00963c4e8310825 was directly read from XLSX and its historical record.

Operator handles physical connection and port photos; no reset/rebind, firmware flash, unapproved write, log clear or automatic retry.
No connection, query, transaction, reset, retry, firmware action or DUT action was executed.

test_case.test_name: Variant-bound USB2/USB3 physical-port topology, negotiated-speed and bounded-function validation
test_case.purpose: Verify each approved USB 2.0/3.x physical port path, hubs and MCU endpoint enumerate the intended fixture at the signed negotiated speed and complete the approved non-destructive function without reset, downgrade or error.
required_package: Source Key/Variant identity and exclusion of the same-code M.2 firmware-flash row
Chassis/internal port-to-controller/root-port/hub/MCU topology and population matrix
Approved cable/device fixture VID:PID/product/serial/interface/driver and supported generations
Per-port USB generation, expected negotiated speed and descriptor/configuration oracle
Fixture-specific bounded non-destructive function, error limits and safe connection/removal procedure
test_case.test_command: For each signed port, the operator connects the approved traceable fixture once using the approved procedure and records the physical label. Collect complete untruncated `lsusb -tv`, full descriptors and timestamped USB kernel events; correlate bus path, hubs, MCU and fixture identity; compare negotiated speed with the per-port matrix; if required, run only the supplied bounded non-destructive functional transaction and preserve its complete result without reset/retry.
test_case.expected_result: Every in-scope physical port maps to the expected controller/hub/MCU path, the exact fixture enumerates with correct descriptors/driver at its signed speed, the approved function completes, and reset/disconnect/overcurrent/protocol errors remain within signed limits.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS only when physical label, full topology, fixture identity, per-port speed and required functional result all match the signed matrix with acceptable errors. Wrong/missing path or device, link downgrade, function failure, reset/flap/overcurrent or error-limit breach is FAIL. Missing topology/fixture/speed/function oracle is BLOCKED at execution; enumeration alone cannot PASS when a function is required.
safety_gate: Gate CLOSED until Source Key/Variant, exact ports/topology, approved fixture, speed/function matrix and connection/recovery procedure are signed.
Operator performs physical connections; inspect power/cable compatibility and never force a connector.
No same-code firmware flash, device reset/rebind, unapproved transfer/write, log clearing, output truncation or automatic retry.
Stop on wrong device/path, overcurrent, heat, repeated reset/disconnect, downgrade, functional error or unstable MCU/management behavior.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash and explicit separation from row 2041 M.2 Firmware-Flash
Per-port physical label/photo and controller/root-port/hub/MCU topology map
Complete timestamped USB tree, descriptors, negotiated speed and kernel events per port
Approved bounded functional-transaction result and error/reset/overcurrent comparison
Safe removal/final state, discrepancies, recovery and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: Stop on wrong identity, overcurrent, heat, reset storm, downgrade or functional error; preserve evidence and have the operator disconnect only by the signed procedure. Leave controllers, hubs and MCU firmware/state unchanged, and do not reset, rebind, flash, reconnect or rerun automatically.
